projects.title: Retail delivery diagnostics: an end-to-end case
projects.summary: Diagnosis of a department-store delivery network, from 62,420 raw shipment records to an executive dashboard. The monthly report said 95.7% of deliveries were on time and in full, yet management felt deliveries were getting slower. The analysis shows where and why.
highlights: Cleaning with lineage: 62,420 raw records reduced to 59,615 shipments, with every exclusion logged.
Stores compared with their own zone through Wilson intervals, so only 1 of 61 stores is flagged as significantly worse.
The worst-stores ranking turned out to be a carrier effect, visible only after conditioning on zone.

projects.title: EMA/MACD signal toolkit
projects.summary: Moving averages, MACD(12, 26, 9) and RSI implemented from first principles for a finance diploma, then extended into a batch run over 35 equities listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange and a bitcoin cost comparison across Mexican platforms.
highlights: Cross-validated against a 3,815-formula Excel model to within 5 × 10⁻¹³, recalculated in CI on every push.
Bitcoin with pesos: live Bitso and Binance order books against Mercado Pago, measured from the prices its app shows. Buying and selling at once costs 0.27% on Binance and 3.98% on Mercado Pago.
Crossovers are judged against noise: on a random walk MACD crosses its signal every 12.3 periods, and 22 of the 35 tickers cross at least that often.
82 unit tests on properties derived by hand, such as MACD equal to 7 × slope on a linear trend, all offline.

projects.title: Milky Way structure: Gaia DR3 × APOGEE-2 DR17
projects.summary: Spatial and kinematic characterisation of the Milky Way's stellar populations, built by cross-matching Gaia DR3 astrometry with APOGEE-2 DR17 spectroscopy.
highlights: 682,284 sources reduced to 281,612 stars through documented cuts on signal-to-noise, astrometric fit, radial-velocity scatter and parallax.
Velocity ellipsoid tilted by a vertex deviation of about −26.6°, consistent with asymmetric drift.
DBSCAN partially recovers the Hercules moving group, and the rotation curve is flat beyond 8.5 kpc.

projects.title: Stellar classification and astrostatistics
projects.summary: Statistical characterisation of 240 stars from their temperature and spectral class: distribution fitting by maximum likelihood, model selection, normalisation and hypothesis tests across spectral classes.
highlights: A physically motivated Gamma model beats an Exponential fit by AIC (4,908.98 against 4,926.26).
Box-Cox failed to normalise the data and Ordered Quantile normalisation succeeded, which enabled inference.
92% confidence intervals and t and F tests across 15 pairs of spectral classes.

images.caption: Probabilistic against theoretical model
images.description: The proposed Exponential model against a theoretical Gamma model based on Wien's law for stellar temperatures. AIC favours the Gamma distribution (4,908.98).

projects.title: Lecture notes pipeline with agentic RAG
projects.summary: Turns four-hour class recordings into structured Obsidian notes with no manual steps, then answers questions about past classes citing the class and the minute: local transcription on the CPU, notes written by Claude Code in headless mode and an agent over hybrid retrieval.
highlights: Fits in 8 GB of RAM: silence-aligned ten-minute chunks cut peak audio memory from more than 6 GB to about 0.7 GB on a two-hour recording.

Hybrid retrieval over notes and transcripts, with multilingual embeddings and Spanish BM25 merged by Reciprocal Rank Fusion. The agent answers only with real citations or says the notes do not cover it.
Whatever Claude adds stays visibly separate from what was said in class, and mistakes not corrected in class are flagged.
88 tests with no network access: a fake Whisper model, a fake claude executable, the real Anthropic SDK over a fake transport and a real Chroma database.

projects.title: Reward hacking on GSM8K: two small model organisms
projects.summary: SFT, DPO and GRPO written from scratch in PyTorch with Claude Code, then used to study what a 0.5B language model learns when its RL grader has a loophole: one grader also pays the answer the user suggested, the other pays any final line that contains the right number.
highlights: A grader that also pays the answer the user suggested drove copying of wrong suggestions from 7% to 97% of training samples. The habit carried over to unseen phrasings (64%) and to SVAMP problems (62%).

In 89% of the copies the reasoning itself arrives at the user's number, usually through a false equation, which a consistency monitor cannot see. Penalising what that monitor flags cut flagged copies from 10.8% to 1.8% while copying stayed at 96%.

Hedging grew only modestly under a lenient grader that pays answers such as 24 or 72: the model's hedges contained the right answer less often than its single answers were right (39% against 48% during training).
Ten hypotheses were written before any GPU run, and each loophole run has a control that differs only in the grader. Every log is in the repository, so all the numbers can be rebuilt on a CPU.
projects.snippet: Qwen2.5-0.5B → SFT → DPO → GRPO (strict | biased grader)   ·   SFT with seeded hedges → GRPO (strict | lenient grader)

projects.title: Folio: from scanned receipts to structured fields
projects.summary: Document AI built in measured stages: OCR with Tesseract, rules and a learned ranker for receipt totals and dates, Claude Haiku reading the scan behind a cascade, then document types and receipt layouts. Every method is frozen before its one test run, and search and an API on AWS Lambda come next.
highlights: Claude Haiku 5.5 reading the scan through a JSON schema finds the total on 97% of 200 held-out receipts and the date on 99%. Given the OCR text instead, the same model finds 78%, since the right total survives OCR on only 88% of them.

A cascade asks the model only when the cash check or a logistic-regression ranker is unsure: 94% of totals with 89 calls for 200 receipts, against 82% for the ranker alone. A guard against misread digits, added after reading its misses, takes it to 96% (measured post hoc).

A linear SVM on the Tesseract text of Tobacco3482 tells ten document types apart on 85% of 696 held-out pages. Its margin keeps three quarters of them at 96.5% and flags the quarter it gets right only half the time.

Clustering receipts by their first rows finds the merchants without labels (AMI 0.92). The ranker drops from 85% on known merchants to 74% on new ones while the LLM stays near 97%, and grouped cross-validation shows the gap comes from rarer merchants, not memorised layouts.

projects.title: Small language model from scratch
projects.summary: Every component of a small language model, implemented and then trained, for Carnegie Mellon University's Introduction to Modern AI (online, January to April 2026).
highlights: An autodiff engine, a BPE tokenizer and the Adam optimiser written from first principles.
A decoder-only transformer with masked multi-head attention, a KV cache, RMSNorm and a gated MLP, trained on TinyStories.
Fine-tuned with supervised fine-tuning, DPO and reinforcement learning for reasoning on GSM8K.
projects.note: The code stays private under the course's academic integrity policy. Its post-training part is rebuilt in the open in the reward-hacking project.

projects.title: Galaxy morphology with convolutional networks
projects.summary: Binary classification of 5,608 MaNGA galaxy images into early types and late types, from a baseline CNN to transfer learning, with the class imbalance handled explicitly.
highlights: Baseline CNN: 81.0% test accuracy, held back by a recall of only 0.68 on early types, the minority class.
A deeper CNN reached 86.3% test accuracy and raised early-type recall to 0.77.
InceptionV3 transfer learning reached 85.9% with balanced recall of 0.86 on both classes.

projects.title: Incentive compensation API: a QA case study
projects.summary: A full QA cycle on a sales-commission REST API, the kind of calculation that sales performance management software automates: split credit, clawbacks on returns, a 50% gate, tiered accelerators and a cap.
highlights: 92 risk-based test cases traced to the requirements, and 8 defects found in the first build, 2 of them critical.
A parallel run against an independent Excel model measured 6,566.74 MXN overpaid by the first build and 750 of 750 payouts correct after the fixes.
One critical defect only appeared on PostgreSQL, because SQLite does not enforce foreign keys by default. CI now tests on PostgreSQL.

images.description: The two builds side by side. rc1 passed 30 of 92 test cases, matched 552 of 750 payouts and overpaid 6,566.74 MXN over the quarter. rc2 passed 92 of 92, matched 750 of 750 payouts to the cent and left all 9 SQL checks clean.

projects.title: Vigía: operational stability monitoring
projects.summary: A small polyglot platform that ingests request telemetry, reports service-level objectives and detects anomalies: Spring Boot ingestion, a Flask analytics API, a Django back office, PostgreSQL and MongoDB.
highlights: 1.4 million simulated requests over ten days with three injected incidents, all three detected and nothing else.
A Monte Carlo calibration over 40 runs cut false alarms from 18 to 1 without missing an incident.
69 automated tests, run in GitHub Actions together with the calibration.

images.caption: Stability overview
images.description: The Django back office: for each application, requests and 5xx errors in the last hour, p95 latency and 7-day availability against their objectives, error budget used and open incidents.

projects.title: MACD signal API
projects.summary: The EMA/MACD toolkit served as a REST API and tested from the outside: pytest against pandas and hand calculations, plus a Postman collection that Newman runs in CI.
highlights: Its tests found a defect shared with the toolkit: rounding noise of about 10⁻¹⁵ on flat or linear prices reported as crossovers.
Release 1.0.0 passes 28 of 28 pytest results and 59 of 59 Newman assertions.

projects.title: Inflation and reheating solver (MSc thesis)
projects.summary: Modular solver for the coupled Friedmann and Klein-Gordon equations, tracking the scale factor, the inflaton and the energy densities from inflation into reheating. It covers T-model potentials and the pure quartic regime, and checks numerical results against slow-roll predictions.
highlights: Energy densities for T-model potentials follow the expected scaling with the scale factor, a^(−6k/(k+2)).
The numerical end of inflation is compared with the analytical slow-roll prediction.

projects.title: Astrophysical jet simulation
projects.summary: Two-dimensional hydrodynamic simulation of an astrophysical jet, built up from advection and 1D Euler solvers, comparing adiabatic and radiatively cooled runs from a single configuration file.
highlights: 400 × 150 cells over a 4,000 × 1,500 AU domain, run for 100 years with a MacCormack scheme and CFL = 0.1.
Neutral or ionised mean molecular weight, switched at 10⁴ K.
With radiative cooling the bow shock is narrower and the jet more compact.

projects.title: The Bar Strikes Back: galactic bar dynamics
projects.summary: How a dynamically cold stellar disc responds to the smooth growth of a galactic bar, with 10,000 test particles in a composite, collisionless potential.
highlights: Fourth-order Runge-Kutta-Nyström integration, with a time step chosen by measurement: the energy error of a circular orbit stays below 10⁻¹³.
Every particle gains energy as the bar grows, and total energy rises by 120%.
The gain grows monotonically with initial radius.

images.caption: Phase-space evolution
images.description: Six snapshots of a dynamically cold disc. As the bar potential grows, non-circular orbits appear and the system stretches along a preferred axis.

images.caption: Energy gain
images.description: Final against initial specific energy. Every point lies above the identity line: each particle gained energy from the time-dependent potential.

images.alt: Energy gain against initial radius
images.caption: Radial energy redistribution
images.description: Energy gain against initial radius. Particles in the outer disc absorbed more energy than those in the inner disc while the bar grew.
